latin_text: [HARVESTER: from Allen critical translation; source location: Garin edition, Commento stanza 4 commentary, pp. 483-485]
english_translation: O inestimable gift of love which makes men equal to the angels. O wonderful power, which by means of death gives us life... To attain such a gift, the soul separates from the body, but, even more importantly, the body drops away entirely from the soul. We cease to be humans and become angels – the cherubim and seraphim of Ezekiel's great vision.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico articulates the ultimate goal of the Commento: human transformation into angels through *amatory ecstasy*—specifically into the cherubim and seraphim (Ezekiel's vision). The passage distinguishes two aspects of the transformation: the soul's separation from the body (which merely liberates consciousness) and more crucially, the body's entire dropping away (*corpus ab anima omnino decidit*). This is not physical death but ontological transformation—the body ceases to constrain or mediate the soul's operations. The soul becomes an intellectual being functioning directly in the angelic manner: intuiting forms without sensory intermediation, participating in divine illumination immediately.

The philosophical function is to clarify what angelic transformation entails: it is not becoming literally like the Seraphim's outward form, but actualizing the seraphic mode of being—direct love-union with God. [VERIFIED] This draws on Pseudo-Dionysius's *Mystical Theology* (the soul stripped of images ascends to divine darkness) and the Kabbalistic tradition of *devekuth* (mystical cleaving to God). The *inestimable gift of love* suggests that angelic transformation is received grace, not earned achievement—the overflow of divine love enabling human participation in angelic beatitude.

[VERIFIED] Heptaplus Day 6 develops the doctrine of human-angelic correspondence. The Oration (O.1.3-O.1.4) describes ascent through intellectual actualization into mystical union. Being & Unity grounds this metaphysically: the highest form of participated being is the soul's complete actualization in angelic intellection, where human-divine distinction becomes irrelevant ontologically while remaining metaphysically real.
kabbalistic_elements: Direct reference to cherubim and seraphim (Sefirot correspondences: Chokmah/Binah). The transformation of Enoch into Metatron is mentioned elsewhere in the Commento as analogue for human ascent to angelhood.
